subtopic: Delivering bad news to a client
subtype: Approach: reviewing the call and adjusting communication cadence [Revision]
passage: Review note after the client call, written by Deepika, delivery manager. I sat in on Chaitanya's call with the client on Tuesday. The client was not angry about the delay itself. They said twice that they had found out late and wanted to hear from us more often. Afterwards Chaitanya and I sat with the team and went through the notes. A weekly email was clearly not enough. We changed it: a short note every Monday and Thursday, three lines each: done, next, worries. Chaitanya wrote the first one that afternoon. A week later the client replied, "This is what I needed," and stopped phoning the account manager directly. I will keep watching for three weeks to check it is not turning into a chore.

qa.q: On which days do the short notes go out?
qa.a: The short notes go out every Monday and Thursday.

qa.q: What was the client feeling about the way they were kept informed?
qa.a: The client felt left in the dark and worried, having found out late and wanting to hear more often.

qa.q: What else could the team do to keep the notes useful, and why?
qa.a: The team could ask the client after a month whether three lines are enough, because the right rhythm may change as the project moves.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya have felt after the client's reply?
qa.a: Chaitanya probably felt relieved and encouraged, since a small change in habit had steadied the relationship.

grounding: Illustrates reviewing a client call, finding the client wanted more frequent updates and switching to short Monday and Thursday notes.
